debates.motion: Does the Kalam cosmological argument show that the universe began to exist, has a cause, and points to a personal creator?

sourceSpan.excerpt: Now since then I have attempted to articulate three arguments in support of the first premise that unpack it a little bit more but still basically rooted in this metaphysical intuition that out of nothing nothing comes and therefore something comes into being there surely has to be a cause that brings it into being.

charity.alternative: A sincere critic may question whether the intuition about being and non-being entails a universal causal principle.
charity.decisiveQualification: Denying or suspending judgment on the premise need not reflect indifference to truth or concern merely for intellectual reputation.

sourceSpan.excerpt: Sometimes we talk about things beginning to exist, but it's a misleading turn of phrase... this underlying material that made up the cup didn't begin to exist... all of the humdrum examples of things around us, they're not new substances that appear on the stage... Whereas, if we're considering the origin of the universe... That's got to be different to the mere rearrangement of pre-existing material.

If you could have an actual infinite number of things, it would result in all sorts of situations that I think are metaphysically impossible. Granted, there is no strict logical contradiction... the claim is that this is metaphysically impossible... Benardete imagines a book... For there is no last page.

I'm not persuaded by these examples... Hilbert's Hotel is strange... merely by shuffling guests around, the hotel can accommodate any number of new guests... it's not quite clear to me that that's enough to say that it couldn't exist... the strange and the impossible are not the same... if there was an infinite hotel, that's what it would be like.

An actually infinite collection of things, if it were created by God, he'd have to create it all at once... even God couldn't create it by simply adding one book at a time because I think it's impossible for an actual infinite to be formed by successive addition... whether one begins at a point and tries to reach infinity... or one never begins but counts down from infinity to ending at the present.

He's explicitly appealing to the symmetry between the two things... But I think that all of those arguments... there's a logical gap between the two... I can't get to the end of the endless, but the countdown I can get to the end of the beginningless... the beginningless thing has an end... the symmetry principle there doesn't really work.

I can imagine the situations where something of not very much power kicks off something that goes on to be quite powerful... an AI that can create... a version of itself that's a bit more clever... until you get to a point of something that's superintelligent... Like a kind of avalanche that's kicked off by something small can result in a big effect.

I don't claim that you can show that the creator of the universe is omnipotent or supremely powerful. The word I use is enormously powerful. And the reason for that is because it brings a universe into being out of nothing... this series of demiurges or intermediate causes cannot be infinite in the past. Has to lead back to a first being that is the absolute creator of everything else that follows.

If it's impersonal, then there's some kind of mechanism... if the necessary and sufficient conditions... were present already for eternity... Why not think that it would have done it... infinite time ago?... But I wonder why can't we just describe it in terms of a kind of indeterministic causation?... It just happened to snap at that point and that's the beginning of time. Why does it have to be personal?

That sort of impersonal indeterministic causation of the universe... We're talking about a non-physical state of affairs and therefore, I think the appropriate category would be a personal explanation because appeal to things like quantum indeterminacy... isn't going to get you the origin of the universe just 13.8 billion years ago... it will either happen from eternity or not at all.

debates.motion: Does the evidence from cosmology, fine-tuning, morality, Jesus' resurrection, and religious experience make Christian theism more reasonable than skeptical atheism?

sourceSpan.excerpt: past events must be finite in number; therefore the universe began to exist and has a transcendent cause

charity.alternative: A past-eternal or physically prior cosmology may evade an absolute beginning, and a nonphysical cause need not be either an abstract object or a mind.
charity.decisiveQualification: The strongest alternative accepts present cosmological evidence while denying that it establishes a global beginning or exhausts the possible kinds of cause.

sourceSpan.excerpt: there are only three possible explanations of this extraordinary fine-tuning: physical necessity, chance, or design

charity.alternative: Chance may operate through observer selection or multiple universes, while apparent parameter freedom may be reduced by deeper physical laws not yet known.
charity.decisiveQualification: The strongest nondesign alternative does not treat the constants as a single unconditioned random draw from a known uniform probability distribution.
